newsitem.title: MEXICO: Left-winger widens lead in Mexico City race - poll.
newsitem.headline: Left-winger widens lead in Mexico City race - poll.

text.p: Left-wing veteran Cuauhtemoc Cardenas has increased his lead over his main challengers in the closely-watched race for mayor of Mexico City, according to a new survey published on Monday.
The survey by Indemerc/Louis Harris gave Cardenas and his Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) 33 percent of voter preferences, up from 32.2 percent in April.
Mexico City voters choose their first elected mayor on July 6. The job carries huge political weight and is widely seen as a "dry run" for the next presidential race in 2000.

Carried out from May 9-14, the survey of 1,138 respondents showed support for Cardenas was not affected by an allegation he had illegally transferred a public beach property to his mother while serving as governor of the state of Michoacan.
The candidate who made the allegation, conservative Carlos Castillo Peraza of the National Action Party (PAN), saw his support slip to 17.2 percent in May from 20 percent in April.
Castillo is now tied with Alfredo del Mazo, the candidate for President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI). His support rose from 14.5 percent in April.
The PRI had been in third place in all of Indemerc's previous surveys but the polling firm predicted there would now be a "big fight for second place".
Last year, before the parties chose their candidates, the PAN were the favourites by far to win the mayor's race.

But the PAN's strongest candidate, former presidential hopeful Diego Fernandez de Cevallos, declined to run and political analysts say the PAN chose the wrong candidate by opting for the acerbic and intellectual Castillo.

Using Indemerc's own method of assigning the likely voting pattern of the 22.2 percent of "don't knows" recorded in the May survey, the pollsters predicted Cardenas would win 44 percent of the vote if the election were held today.
Castillo and the PAN would win 22.19 percent and the PRI would garner 21.25 percent, Indemerc predicted.
It gave a margin of error of 3.5 percent for the survey.
